utterances.text: All right. There's no difficulties about that. I've just got a couple of more questions -- returning to Prozor now. As to the killed people that you saw there you noticed no one who had been shot in the head; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: As far as I could see. There appeared to be all torso wounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you noticed no one had been shot more than twice; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I didn't find a body which had more than two bullet wounds in it, but I didn't inspect all of the bodies. So I can't say that one didn't have more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of the bodies did you inspect?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: About six or seven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the video that you've seen, are you able to identify the -- by reference to the blankets and any other identifying mark those bodies which you did look at?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever provided with a name of any of those bodies that you looked at?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- did you have anyone either among the British party or -- or indeed any person at all who was able to speak both English and Bosnian, Serbian, Croatian?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: The British army had an interpreter with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And was that person prepared to assist you with questions if you asked them?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was a British army soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact did that person assist you with questions from time to time when you asked?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: From time to time, but there were few people who were worth questioning, and by that I'm not being patronising. My point about questions is that unless I have eyewitnesses, the testimony for me is secondhand and I have to treat it carefully. And particularly for this kind of instance. I was looking all time for an eyewitness and I did not find one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to the -- to the Croatian militia persons that you've described, did the -- do you have the interpreter ask any of them whether they were eyewitnesses or not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: They appeared not to have been eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, but the question is did you get the interpreter to put that precise question to --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: It was not as precise. These are not formal circumstances because we are moving around a room with dead bodies. We have distraught people outside. We are being extremely careful. Occasionally one -- one says, does anybody -- is anybody saying so and so, is does anybody giving this information? But I'm extremely aware that there is no eyewitness coming forward which is -- as a reporter what I'm very aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, and don't take my questions to contain criticisms, but I have to ask the question in a precise way for later transcript purposes, and the question is: Did you get the interpreter to ask any of these young Croatian soldiers whether they were eyewitnesses or not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I think I was aware that the information had come to me already that they were not eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in a general sense when you're in the field like that you're receiving information from various people, soldiers nearby, your cameraman, anyone else who's -- who might have noticed something; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: You take information from wherever you can but you have to evaluate it and you have to be aware as we were in all of the time in Bosnia that most of the people living near or close experience to something like this frequently do not tell the truth, particularly if they have not been eyewitnesses. The reasons are obvious and manifold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's turn from the journey from Prozor down to Uzdol. In the course of that journey you indicated that you noticed a person -- well, perhaps I should ask you, did you see more than one person dead in the fields or the countryside nearby?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Two. Two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: We saw two bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were both of those -- can I just ask you a couple of questions about that, were both of those persons depicted in the film that we've seen here?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes, one is in the transmission, and the other is in the second shot which you saw in the -- secondly, the extra rushes at the end.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly pause between question and answer, and please speak one at a time to ensure an accurate record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I consider myself ticked off by the interpreters, Your Honour, and I will endeavour to do better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pardon me, Ms. Adie. So -- where was I? Very well. As to either of those people, were both of them in the same position, namely that it was potentially dangerous to approach them closely?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There used to be a lot of scare-mongering in -- by local people, that there were mines in areas where there was some kind of activity. "Minar, minar," [sic] people used to shout. It -- it happened sometimes there -- and there were some booby-trapped areas, field, doorways, gates to field. The British army like any professional army was always extremely careful about approaching a body that was in the public view, again because of booby-traps or any kind of problems surrounding it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just as to those two people, I take it, then, that for very good and sensible reasons you didn't approach them or inspect the bodies?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No. But my cameraman zoomed in on one of them and could tell that it was a civilian lying in a field as if he had been --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Been shot?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Died unexpectedly, and been shot would be the obvious one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And when you say civilian, you're unaware of whether those individuals who were in the field belonged to any particular organisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: They looked like locals. The man was wearing rough clothes of a farmer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: And I think a cap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were you aware of whether or not any of the locals in their rough suits and caps were members of the Home Guard of the HVO or not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I do not recognise this phrase "Home Guard," and you're suggesting organisation, which would barely have been able to exist in the chaos and lack of administration in Bosnia at the time. You're suggesting something far more organised than anything we ever encountered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to take you now to certain of the facts in -- or certain of the observations you made in the village, but before I do that I have to ask you some questions which are general in nature, narrative in nature, and you may say you know or you may say you don't know but I'll put them to you anyway. Did you know that in July of 1993 that civilians in the Uzdol village had been told by the HVO to leave?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I did not know that specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you know in fact that most of the children of school age had in fact indeed left and gone to Prozor and a couple of other villages nearby?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I did not know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of whether or not there were various fortifications stationed around the edges of the hamlets making up the village of Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Can you describe what you mean by fortification?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there's various different types. I'll certainly clarify, but just in general terms were you told that there were any areas that were -- had trenches constructed there?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: We were not told -- you're describing a kind of organisation and precision that did not exist throughout Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So as far as you knew, anyway, that there was no trenches or gun emplacements in the area of Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I was not aware. The British army could tell you because it had fairly specific knowledge of these things. And if there had been, the British army would have warned us about any major emplacements if we were going into that area, and the officer in charge would have known and would have had that intelligence. We had special services and intelligence on the ground for the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And when you got to Uzdol, did you notice the remains of a tank, an army tank near the school?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you there had been an army tank there that had unfortunately been destroyed the previous day?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No. It was -- nobody mentioned that. Interesting that a tank got up there. That's all I would say. I couldn't see the point of it, really, from tactical terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: That's -- sorry. That's speculation. But it wouldn't be what I was looking for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. But it's a bit hard to miss a tank if it was there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, you're wrong. It's extremely easy to conceal one in that kind of countryside and behind ruins. Two trees and a bit of earth and you can do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- but in fact the answer to my question basically is this, that you didn't see a tank and no one pointed out the existence of one?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as to wrecked buildings, did you see any buildings that were wrecked?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes a couple were. They had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And did you see any that were still burning?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There was a smouldering building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any that had obviously been destroyed by some agency or another.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Burning only. There were no major shell holes, mortar holes, or anything resembling any large, heavy weaponry being fired at all. Nor were there any what we called "splat marks." This is journalistic term for shell damage against the walls of large buildings which were common to half of Bosnia or more. There was only small-arms fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the buildings that were actually on fire or damaged? Did you inspect those to see whether they --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: The timber had gone and they had fallen in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in short, it's impossible to draw any conclusion as to whether they'd been hit by artillery fire so far as you're --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There was absolutely zero evidence of artillery fire to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of those burnt houses there, was any evidence of anything that had caused them to burn?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I saw several houses set on fire during ethnic cleansing which involved usually the use of some petrol and a match.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you notice any petrol being used on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: You would not find the evidence unless you were doing a forensic investigation, and it would be difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say it would be difficult, do you -- were you able to smell any petrol at any of these burnt buildings?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: You don't. Any forensic scientist would tell you that afterwards in the countryside 24 hours later. I saw several buildings being set alights in the three years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you this -- sorry. Just?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: You just set them alight with whatever material is available. Maybe I should not have mention the petrol. You use the curtains, you use the materials inside. You use perhaps straw from the farm outside. It is extremely easy, particularly in houses which have a lot of wood, and as I also indicated a lot of wooden furniture inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But the point is this, that you didn't smell any petrol; right?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I perhaps -- if I could withdraw the phrase petrol because I said it just on the -- having seen it used a couple of times in other villages but that other -- yet at other times I saw other much simpler ways of setting a house on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Were you told whether or not there were active armed HVO soldiers living in the hamlets that went to make up Uzdol on the night of the attack?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I was told no information like that. I could comment on the assumption that there might be, but there was no information came to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. I don't want you to comment on assumptions, but did you ask that question through the interpreter, "were there active armed soldiers in the village at the time when the killings took place"?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There was almost no one around who could give such an answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Croats?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: The Croats, we had country boys who did not have specific information, who were clearly local, and who clearly did not have any detailed information of any major operations. These were local lads, and as a --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you ask them?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: -- as a journalist, you don't -- we had limited time and it's not the kind of question which would have produced an honest answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's just take that step-by-step. First of all, you didn't ask them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry that's my silly question there. Did you ask them?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Sorry. All right. And is the reason you didn't ask them because they were local people and you didn't think you'd get a truthful answer?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I ask questions of people under certain circumstances when I think that there will -- it would be valid to listen to them, not whether it is truthful or not. In this instance, we had a lot of dead Croat people, and I made the assumption that people wearing Croat uniform would give me an answer which would frame their view of what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you interview that Croat soldier on the BBC if that's the case?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Because he claimed to know the family, and that was a claim which I thought could be either later found to be true or false. That to me was a link to an eyewitness piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you find out whether it was true or false later?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What checks did you do to try to find that out?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I did not need to do that. It is not part of my remit. I am not an investigator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And were you told -- well, perhaps just in terms of asking these questions, did it appear to you be a relevant thing to question about whether there had been military conflict in the village or whether it had just been a simple -- well, not simple I suppose, that's an unfair question. Did it -- I'll ask the question again. Did it seem to you to be important to verify whether there had been a military fight on the one hand or a piece of brutal ethnic cleansing on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes, I did think that important, and I found that was what was already -- was in the report as you have seen. I could not fully verify this in any way, shape, or form, except that the British military, having had a good look round the school building, indicated that there had been, and the phrase they gave to me, "some kind of rear guard action."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But just returning to the Croatian boys or young men that you've indicated. Let me be quite clear about the position. Not only did you not ask them through the interpreter, but you're not aware of anyone else asking them either through the interpreter or directly as to whether there was a military action in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: They were not eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Because I knew that I had no eyewitnesses. That I did know from the Prozor -- no one was there who had witnessed what had happened. That had been my first inquiry. Is there anyone here who knows and saw, saw what happened? And at the very beginning we knew that no one claimed to have been there at the time of the killing of the elderly people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- and how did you know that, that no one had been there at the time of the killing of the elderly people?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Because when we got to Prozor we said, "Did anyone see this happen," and the answer was "No."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask whether there were any survivors?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes, and as far as I -- and this was in my report we -- as far as we could find out there were none. No one came to us either and -- and with the circumstances, when we were in Prozor, if you have a number of bodies laid out and the Croats are happy enough for us to view the dead bodies, both British military and journalists, and I've known of instances where these things have been covered up, if they were happy for us to see the dead bodies, I think they would have been more than happy to produce someone who saw what had happened and had been a survivor. I would have thought that's automatic in this situation, and we had no one come forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. But just come back to the question. The question I asked you was: "Did you ask whether there were any survivors," and you answered me "Yes," and then you went on to explain the inference that you drew. But I just want to deal with that answer of yes. Who did you ask whether there were any survivors?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There was what -- sorry. You are suggesting a formal interview situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you who you asked?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I was talking with the army interpreter who was gleaning, and that is the phrase I was using, gleaning snippets of information from people, and I was asking him fairly direct questions which he would be aware of anyway because his officer and the two EU monitors were also asking. We were all asking, "Did anyone see what happened? Have we got an eyewitness?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the answer?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: The answer came back, "No we didn't."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did that answer come back from?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Via the interpreter from all the people who he was going around talking to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those people were the soldiers in uniform and certain local civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So at the very least what we can say is the soldiers were telling you, or those you were with, that there were no survivors; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: They didn't say that precisely. They didn't produce a survivor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a second. Let's be clear about this. Did they say that there was an eyewitness in existence or did they say there was no eyewitness in existence?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: They said neither. They didn't produce one. When you ask a roomful of people, did anyone see anything and they put their arms in the air and shake their heads and no one comes forward. You are in -- keep presuming precise questions. This was not the circumstance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as a barrister I can well understand it. It's not always right -- it's not always possible to ask a direct question, isn't it? In my case, you have all sorts of reasons. But you're an experienced journalist and you know how to ask a direct question. Now what I'm asking you is: Why didn't you put it to some of the soldiers, "Listen, have you got an eyewitness or not"?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I didn't need to. I already knew by the first two minutes in that room that no one was going to come forward. I have been in circumstances time and again where I have arrived as a journalist and if people on one particular side wish to deliver full information about what has happened, which will give full information as to what has happened to their people as victims, they will produce, they will push forward, they will name, they will indicate or they will in some way deliver an eyewitness to you because it is in their favour if they do it. If they don't then you can make the assumption that there is no eyewitness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is that the assumption that you drew?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: It was at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And certainly nobody mentioned to you that there was a person called Kazimir Zelenika who might be of interest?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Specific names are rarely mentioned in these instances by local people in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any specific names given to you?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Only the one given by the Croat up at Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that was the one who pointed to the name of Ratkic?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- very well. As to other questions about that, did you make any inquiries of Croat armed forces, the HVO, or any other force whether they had in fact shelled, fired artillery fire on the morning when the killings took place?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Such inquiries were not made by journalists because they were fruitless and pointless, and nor was there an obvious headquarters of an organisation to inquire of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the senior Croatian military person that you met down at -- either at Prozor or at Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No senior military people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone who seemed able to call the shots with the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there no one with the insignia or any -- any indication that they had a position of seniority?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: All of these things were meaningless in the terms of the militias operating in Bosnia in rural areas. They called themselves generals when they were corporals. We used occasionally the term commander when someone said they had responsibility for a particular unit. Other than that, it was toy-town military nonsense, I have to say. And I'm just trying to point out that the kind of organisation you're presenting to me was not obvious to us in any sense on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, a minute ago I was asking you questions about fortifications and so on around the village of Uzdol and you gave certain answers there. Specifically was a -- an area of entrenchments with the name Borak draw to your attention at any stage?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any other strong points, for want of a better word, placed within 500 metres of the emplacement at Borak drawn to your attention?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Strong point? Can you describe what I should be looking for? I'm genuinely -- I don't know what you mean there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm in your hands to some degree here. The answer might well be simply, no, you weren't told anything about it but?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: What am I looking for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're looking for entrenchments, places where soldiers guard the front line.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Such trenches were dug in some areas, but hit and run tactics were the most common, and for a strong point where a gun emplacement might be, because guns were so hard to come by on most sides, they were usually moved from one position to another. So you're not looking for permanent positions most of the time in Bosnia. Rare to find them. Rare to see any earthworks or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, well I'm really specifically dealing with Uzdol here, if that's okay. Is the answer to my question that No, no one told you about any such --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Nor would we be looking at because this was not a flashpoint area of huge tactical significance unlike, for example, Gornji Vakuf which was a front line fight between two very close groups of fighters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Prozor did not have that kind of action around it from the very early days when most of the Bosnians had been driven out by burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of whether or not the Bosnian army was conducting a series ever attacks along a series of axes along the 13th and 14th of -- of September?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: The Bosnian army was a collection -- the Army of BiH was a collection in 1993 of a ragtag group of disparate units which had poor communication, if any, and uncoordinated behaviour area by area. The idea that it was a wholly coordinating, communicating army is unknown to me. So the idea that a specific act was carried out may have happened in an area but it was unknown to me and I certainly wouldn't see it as part of an overarching strategy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your experience that army consisted of a lot of self-willed little warlords who obeyed when they felt like it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Not entirely. I had connections with both -- and I saw and knew commanders up in Travnik and in Zenica it was the 3rd Corps and with the 2nd Corps in Tuzla. They lacked all kinds of essentials for a functioning army. There was some extremely well-disciplined men. I specifically remember one commander, two commanders, one in Travnik, one in Zenica. There were others who acted as warlords and so on. This was common to both the Croats and the Serbs and the Bosnian Muslims, with the Bosnian Muslims having the greater problem of fewer resources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But just coming back to the specifics of the battle you weren't aware of any --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Battle? "Battle" is not a word I would use. Battle is a large-scale, coordinated military operation, hardly ever seen in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand we're not discussing Waterloo here, but perhaps we could just use the word "battle" in its broader sense?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, because you misunderstand the nature of fighting in Bosnia which was like domestic violence on a village and town scale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Well, do you know a hill called Crni Vrh?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Makljan.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was an attack made by Bosnian Muslim units who, in an attempt to took over the hill Crni Vrh on the way to --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Well, Crni Vrh would mean black hill, I believe, and there must be a thousand of those in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, well we're talking about the one on the road to Makljan here, so what's your answer? Do you know whether there was an attack there or not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I don't know the word of Mak -- can you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Makljan, a town.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Town, big town?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Either it's unknown to me, or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- I think --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Not as big as Prozor. Prozor is a tiny country town, anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, anyway, I take it that you --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I'm generally ignorant about this. I don't know where you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I'm not being critical in any way. It's just -- I just needed to know whether you were aware of -- of any military action in that area, and I suppose your answer is you don't even know the town of Makljan, so that puts an end to those questions.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yeah. It doesn't sound -- it's not a big town that I've heard it. So --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Can I say that we used to get, and this refers back to the first question you asked me at the very beginning. We used to get information from all kinds of sources, some of it first hand, some of it fourth hand, about activity, if I can put it in inverted commas, all over the region on a daily basis. Some of it was significant, some of it was -- didn't even happen. So unless we actually got to an area which was why for example I went to Uzdol, which I thought was significant, we tended not to give a great deal of credence to various reported so-called military actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can I just ask you whether you -- I understand what you say about the -- about the military -- whether they're battles or not, but --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Can I also point out something about Prozor which I think is relevant here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course of course?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Prozor was one -- on one of the main supply routes, MSRs, up from the coast to the Lasva Valley to Zenica, big town, and then onwards to Tuzla. It was one of the army-patrolled routes for NATO and previously the UN. It was a main road and a real artery going through Central Bosnia. If there had been major military activity within even five, six miles, ten miles of that road we would have all have been alerted to it over the period of time we were there in -- because that would have possibly cut that main supply route. I cannot remember any major point except north of Prozor near Gornji Vakuf where an artillery piece appeared somewhere in early 1993 of any specific problem that ever closed the road or made it a risk road. So major activity near it would seem to be -- it would be much more minor, local fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question on that is did the British intelligence services ever miss anything around that time?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: You must ask them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, look what we might do now is turn to the -- turn to the issue of -- of the -- what you saw when you got to Uzdol. First of all, is it your -- I'm sorry. Is it your understanding that Uzdol consisted of three or four hamlets?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes, because when we enquired of the name of the village, in inverted commas, there was various points to go various areas and the area appeared to be called Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I don't know whether you got this specific but I have to put the questions to you. Did you become aware of a village -- of a hamlet called Kriz, K-r-i-z?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask for specific names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Uzdol appeared to me to be a generic name for that little region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay well I just -- I'm going to put some specifics to you anyway, and they may jog your memory and they may not. But I mentioned Kriz what about Rajici, R-a-j-i-c-i?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I have to say that's quite a common name in Bosnia. So if I did remember it would be possibly because I've heard it elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What about Cer?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, not the football team. Z-e-l-e-n-i-k-a?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes. The reason for that being that in television-reporting terms I would only use a minimum of designated place names and sometimes specific personal names because we don't scatter names in the -- in the report. We keep it fairly simple.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it -- is it a possible -- well, there's a photograph we could show you and it might assist, I don't know if it will. Are you able to recall the route that you took when you were in the village?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Coming to the village, what I remember is that we had on our right we were coming up a ridge line heading east and the -- as we curved around towards it the school was at the top of the ridge on a -- slightly to our right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was on the way from Prozor?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go through a village called Donja Vas on the way?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: None of them have village signs. We did not stop to ask. We are in armoured vehicles and it is an unknown area so we do not ask directions and names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, now, apart from -- I'm now going to take you some of the killed people that you saw and I've got some specific questions about them, but apart from the -- the people described to you as having the surname Ratkic, were there any others who -- to whom was attributed a name that was told to you?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did any of the soldiers, I'll call them militiamen if you're happy with that term, any of the Croatian militiamen that you saw point out any of those people and give names to them even though they weren't relayed on to you?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No. I would not be looking for specific names. I'm assuming that -- because I would not be using them in my report. And secondly, they appear to have been killed in their own homes, so for later reasons, people would be able to identify them. There are instances where I've been at stories where bodies have been found in various circumstances and you've needed identity perhaps to help inquiries afterwards. Theses people appeared to be in their own homes in their home village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- you did not want to name them?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I did not need to name them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why was it that you went to such lengths to interview that soldiers because -- simply because he could name the name of Ratkic?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I didn't go to any great lengths. You misconstrue the work of a reporter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put another question, then. Why was it that you asked the questions there of that soldier -- just a minute. Why did you ask those questions of that soldier on the basis that he knew the names of the Ratkics?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Well, you've answered the question. He said who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So putting the names on national TV was a good idea; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Not at all. You misconstrue the nature of it. The reason for doing that kind of interview is to identify as a specific person with a name someone which stands generically therefore for identifying people in the village. That is a common, as it were, technique we would use in television, that we have got someone who is prepared to give a name, identify, and therefore it stands for us being able to identify people in the village. But we do not go round and do it with every family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then is your position this, that -- well, perhaps I could ask you this: Why was it that you asked about the Ratkics and were interested by the name, in the case of the Ratkics but didn't pursue that question in the relation to the other killed people?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I thought I just answered that. But let me make it clear again. I'm going to repeat myself, that if you interview someone in a crowd at a football match, you might ask a particular football fan what he thought of it and you would ask for his name to identify and verify his identity and the authenticity of the interview. You Do not ask the other 37.000 people in the crowd what their names are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't ask this soldier his name, you asked him the name of the people who were -- who he was identifying. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Look, anyway --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: He said he was related to them and he knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you notice whether or not the man Ratkic who was the deceased man did -- was he mutilated by having his ears cut off when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: That is an old folk superstition that knocks around Bosnia a lot, and if I knew of evidence of that I would look for the evidence. It was not mentioned at the time, and no one pointed it out to me nor did I see any evidence myself. But they had been burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just to be clear about this, you said in your statement to the OTP this: "I did not see any mutilated or tortured or beaten or burnt bodies," and that was accurate, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, turning to mutilated, you would understand -- this is -- I'm not being condescending about this, I just have to put the question in a step-by-step way. You would understand cutting off someone's ears to be mutilation, quite simple?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There is a long and primitive tradition in many countries and it arose in the Balkans at various times of various forms of mutilation and allegations of mutilation, sometimes which was proved but was often found to be completely fanciful. But it is a product of a folk tradition, and the cutting off of noses and ears, fingers, particularly children's or baby's fingers, is a tale heard over and over again in the Balkans from the -- 1991 onwards. If we heard this and someone alleged it, you tried to find the evidence. It was extremely rare that any journalist saw this. It was told to us over and over again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the concrete case of Martin Ratkic whose body you saw apparently in the arms of a woman, and killed, you didn't notice that he had his ears cut off, did you?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No one mentioned to me that the ears had been cut off, and therefore I did not look to the body to notice it. I mean, we could possibly look at the video again to see. There would have been therefore a great display of blood, I would assume, if both ears had been cut off. There would be serious amounts of blood loss.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm going to take you through it and we will indeed pause to -- to have a look at that, but certainly at the time when you were -- when you were looking, no one pointed out to you -- we're about to see an example of that folk practice or however it's described?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No one mentioned it, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I wonder now if we could play the video which is P373. I'm just going to have to ask that this be stopped at certain moments, and, Ms. Adie, what I'll do is stop at particular parts and ask you to comment on a variety of -- of sights.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure it's the court staff that's going to help or those in the audio-visual booth or it may be that it's the Prosecution because this is going through Sanction. In fact, I think it is -- the Prosecutors who handle it. Could I just request therefore that when I -- Your Honours, this might take a little time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is -- pardon me, Ms. Adie, you'll just have to excuse me while I make arrangements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I've got in mind is to take the witness to particular killed persons and to get her comment about particular aspects of that, so I'll be asking that the tape be stopped on a couple of occasions. Yes, very well. Could we commence that now and we'll -- we'll stop when I call out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "The village of Uzdol is high in the hills of Central Bosnia. It has a school building, lately used as the local Croat military headquarters."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stop there for a moment, please. Thank you. We don't have to go backwards. I just have a question to you about the school. As to the school, were you shown the upstairs part of the school?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you shown any communications equipment that was located in the school?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: The school appeared to be virtually empty on the ground floor that -- what we saw of things, virtually empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And as to whether there was a communications centre up stairs you are unable to comment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: What are we talking about? I don't even recognise the term in the terms of rural militia. Communications that I only ever saw any of these units use would be one small field telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it may be -- it may be that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down, Mr. Morrissey, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps what I'm thinking about is uniformed members of the HVO with radios.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There would be none upstairs at the time because a visit by the British army would have sent them straight into the hills with such stuff, let me tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there something improper about them having communications equipment?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: They would not wish to show anything to the British army. That would be the standard view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well let's --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: And there were certainly no soldiers around. The British went through the buildings and they would have come across anything like that and told us and we would have seen it. And they did a thorough search of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you're concerned at the time you got down to the school there had been -- there was no communications equipment there and no weapons there and, in fact, no soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: If there had been weapons the British would have searched for those initially, that is the standard army practice going into a village which may possibly be hostile or active, and the soldiers would have searched ought rooms for such things, any armed men any weapons any stores of ammunition. Any such matters would have been discovered and would have been reported to us for our own safety and would have been reported to the British army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. Okay. Well, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: So you can assume that they found nothing upstairs, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Of course. Now, moving to the picture that's on the screen in front of you, do you notice that there's a house that's in -- it's a renovator's dream on the right-hand side of that photograph. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: It's a standard post-burning Bosnian house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And it's -- it's quite clear that there's smoke coming from inside the house and also perhaps from a source just to the left of that house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: It's impossible with a burning house to say from that distance where that is, I can tell you, because there could have been a store of wood against the wall. There could have been a sofa against the wall on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but it does look -- well, perhaps I'll put this question to you. You with such knowledge as you've gained over the years in -- as a war reporter cannot comment on what it was that started the fire in that house, can you?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: It's unlikely to have been a bolt of lightning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, well, it might not have been a bolt of lightning, but just as a British journalist, you wouldn't be wanting to comment on what started that, would you?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: In Bosnia houses on fire was such a common occurrence that inquiries as to the cause became relatively pointless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I just note for the transcript, Your Honours, that when Ms. Adie was asked questions about that particular picture it's at 00.16.6 on the transcript, in case we need to come back to that at a later stage can we just proceed now? Very well. Now could we just proceed now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "... army descended on Uzdol than withdrew leaving terrible" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop there, please. Right. Now, we've stopped there tape now at 00.22.3. Now here is depicted a deceased person wrapped in a pink and perhaps brown-looking blanket. Do you recall that particular person independently of the photographs that are here now or not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- it's okay, I mean, but the questions are sometimes, you know, phrased in a -- in a -- in the wrong way. So I'll try to get a --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay, not a problem. With respect to that person there, obviously you can see them depicted on the on the -- on the -- on the --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- on the screen there, and the video. Can you remember anything else about that appearance of that person other than what is on the video in front of them?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other details about that person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No. I look at that. I know that someone has put a blanket round him. I therefore have to ask myself who has done that and that the body has been interfered with since it was killed. That I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you state now what wounds that particular that individual had?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I did not undo any of the blanket on that. The person appears to be bleeding from the mouth, suggesting to me that he has a torso wound which has killed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: He also appears to have died quickly in the positions that his arms and fists are. That is an assumption, but it suggests that he has not lain on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I'll have to ask you just to remain with the -- not with the inferences that you draw --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Okay thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- but with the facts that you observe. Now, do you recall whether you noticed a bullet wound on that person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Although I believe at the top of that blanket there may be some blood. But it's difficult to tell with the colour of the blanket. But I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. That's okay, I'm just talking about what you observed at the time rather than what that we can glean from the photo. So with respect to that person, I was going to ask you about the number of wounds but your situation is that you can't be sure?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, and you don't go too near a body in a field like that which has been interfered with which could have -- possibly be booby-trapped. That was one of the first ones that we actually took pictures of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. Okay, can we please now press on to the next scene? [Videotape played]. "We walked through the scattered farms and cottages with British soldiers and European monitors" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop there for a moment, please. Please stop here. Thank you. Now, this particular house was self-evidently the subject of some sort of fire and has some fire damage on the outside. Can you remember anything about the appearance of that house apart from what's depicted on the screen here and, if it's depicted anywhere else, what?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There are the roof tiles coming off. That is a fierce blaze which has come from the inside on that side of the house because of the scorch marks coming up from the windows. The roof tiles have slid off the guttering suggesting that the interior of the house has gone up and that the roof has collapsed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. These --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is 00.32 on the tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just -- I understand your comments about what can be inferred from that. What I'm asking you now, though, is do you recall anything extra about that house than what is depicted on the pictures?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: In what way? Please guide me. I don't know what you're asking for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any way, do you have a memory of that house outside of what you see on -- on the screen there?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Without another shot of it, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, look, could I ask just ask you to bear that in mind. If you see another shot that jogs your memory about that, feel free to interrupt me and say so because it may be that it's depicted again, it may be that it's not. Anyway, just having regard to that particular house, the last question is: Is that the same house that we saw on the panoramic shot earlier on or how not sure?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: The panoramic shot is of the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It was the shot just after that we saw the burning house. Is this that same burning house that we saw?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, that is not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Very well. Could we keep going now? [Videotape played]. "It soon became clear that every house and cottage and house had been visited by the Bosnian army soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Stop there, please. Sorry, could we go back -- before we come to this bloodstain on the wall, could we just please go back to that previous killed person. [Videotape played]. "It soon became clear that every house and cottage had been visited by the Bosnian army soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Stop there, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- were you ever given a name of that person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No the.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told who wrapped them up in that blanket?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, we were not. All the bodies in Prozor were wrapped in blankets, so we had to assume that some kind of operation had taken place between the killings and the bodies first being shown to us in Prozor at 9.00 that morning and having been transported there, and the blankets are typical, rough Bosnian blankets, and we had no idea who had done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you ask any of the soldiers, the young soldiers who you were with who had done that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as to that killed person there, did you inspect to see what -- I understand you're not a scientist and I'm not asking you to do an off-the-cuff pathology report here, Ms. Adie, and I apologise, sometimes I put you on the spot with these things. But to your observation, did you notice whether she'd been shot or hit or what had occurred to her in terms of --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Been shot. Shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There was blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many -- did you notice any --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, I can't tell you how many, but it definitely a bullet wound. Because there's no other -- there's no other damage to clothing, nor to her face which would happen in an explosion, for example, or a bombing or a mortar blast. The face and hands are clear, so therefore you're looking for a torso wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you notice the specific wound yourself when you saw this person killed?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I didn't take the -- I had a look closely. There was blood; I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't identify a particular bullet wound; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Nor can you say how many bullet wounds that person may have?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Not specifically on that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's at 00.37.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, did you notice any particular amount of blood on that carpet that can be seen in the photograph --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I think it's underneath her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- at the time. Well, the question is there may be blood underneath or there may not be, according to the photograph. But I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I don't think there was blood elsewhere on the carpet in that room, though my memory now is hazy, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: But it's specifically -- what I was looking for was to see whether these bodies -- I know this sounds gruesome, but had been arranged in any way. It's something which you are aware of when you're looking, in quite difficult circumstances, you're going from house to house. You're looking to see if they - to use an awful word - have been posed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: And it seemed to me that they had not. They appeared to have been wrapped probably by someone just lifting up the legs, popping a blanket around them. But the very -- the position across the doorway to me seemed -- there was no sign of it being dragged or of any blood trails along the carpet which you might have had had a body been moved from one place to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The real question I have is -- is did you notice any blood immediately underneath this person or can you not now recall?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, I don't know. But there was no blood elsewhere and there's no blood trail leading to that body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. There is some brownish marks on the doorstep there. I don't know if you can comment --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No, they're not blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- upon those?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: They're not blood. They are -- they are walls in the -- they are -- whatever the word is for -- I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wood holes.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes, in the blood -- in the wood, yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, do you have a specific memory of those marks on that doorstep thing there or not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that you should.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Sorry, Your Honours, I'm just prompted that it might be time for a break but I'm happy to continue, and it's a matter for the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it depends how long we're going to use for this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We're going to go through each person depicted on it, so it will take as long it's now taking. Perhaps, you know, two or three minutes per person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break for 30 minutes and then we'll resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey. Let's continue with the videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just -- sorry, Ms. Adie, do you have the screen with the body with the red and green blanket?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask the Prosecutor to assist by commencing to replay this again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were there, there was no sign of the person who -- whose blood that was that's been placed on the wall there --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- is that correct? Were there any people in that -- were there any people, deceased people of any sort in that particular house when you went there?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I can't remember, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was -- we know from other evidence that a young girl was found and was -- we've seen other videos, of course, in that house. Does that jog your memory in any way? Young girl perhaps about 10?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Well, that would be the one young girl perhaps who was in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At Prozor. We have -- unfortunately, we have two young girls in this case. But in any event, there was no such young girl in this house to --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Not in the house, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, okay. Thanks. Very well. Would you mind -- we've also had some -- do you remember whether there was any bullets, bullet marks in that house outside of that room?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I can't remember. There were very few bullet -- the houses generally is all I could say were not sprayed with bullets, which used to be common in any firefight in Bosnia. They were rather specific, and I think when we looked at the wall of the preceding picture there were no bullets above or around the room. It is a common habit of people to spray round a room if they are going into it in an assault attack. That would be a standard piece of behaviour. There was none of that. This is -- and the bullets here were concentrated in a corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We had some evidence from a man called Kazo Zelenika -- sorry. We had anyway from a particular witness who was associated with this house about noticing quite a lot of bullet fire around. But could I just ask you -- perhaps I'll look -- that was turning into a speech. I'll try another question. When -- when was it that you would inspect a particular wall for -- for bullet marks? Did you look at all the walls in the village or was it just when there was a deceased person or a blood mark such as that nearby that you would turn your mind to the question of bullet marks on walls?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Neither of those instances. On walking through the village, I took note of whether there appeared to be evidence of a major firefight, and particularly as we went into a house I looked for evidence of assault on the building and the classic techniques that anybody would use who had an assault rifle or was going into a house expecting defensive measures to be taken against them, and there was no evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever given -- well, at the time, I should ask you, were you given information that any HVO soldiers who had spent the night sleeping in a house had opened fire on the invading forces?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Had spent which night sleeping in a house?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The night before the killings.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: The night before the killings. There was -- all I can say is there was no evidence of a firefight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. But really, through your interpreter or any of the other people nearby, did anyone nearby mention that any HVO soldiers had returned fire or initiated fire or --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- fired at all?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And incidently, did any of them tell you whether civilians had hand grenades this their houses?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Hand grenades were almost unknown in a domestic setting, and they were very rarely used by any of the forces. That would be a rare instance where a hand grenade was used. The JNA would have been issued with it, one assumes, but the Croats and Muslims, I do not know of an instance, specific instance where we commonly found hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they take you to any houses associated with --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Nor was there any evidence here of a hand grenade being used. You would know instantly from the fragmentation which I have seen endlessly in Beirut of what a hand grenade does and we -- I would know its marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a house associated with a family named Zelic at any stage?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: As you know, I only knew the one name that was given to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's press on from that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we just note that this is 00.48. Now, the deceased person depicted here, can you recall what injuries, if any, you noticed on that person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Bullet wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I think the bullet wound there is somewhere below the right clavicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall actually seeing that at the time?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so far as you could see, that was a single bullet wound?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I only saw one bullet wound. I didn't look for another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the person covered by the blanket when you first got there or not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Because you can also see that there is no bloodstain on that cream part of that blanket there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you notice any bloodstain on the grass underneath that person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There may have been. I cannot recall. The blood would have dried by then, well dried. It's not a huge spill of blood over the actual chest, but it suggests that he was -- that he was on the ground when the bleeding started. Otherwise, the blood would be right down the front of the shirt, I'm assuming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you say -- okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall -- in any event, what you say is that you can't recall whether there's any blood on the grass itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I don't know. It would have soaked away anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, can we please -- and, sorry, just for completeness, you were never told the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And nor did you ask?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I did not ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I also note that the walls behind have two pockmarks, possibly three, on them of stray bullets but that the windows are there, and there is nothing on the side of the wall or anywhere else in the house to indicate other than maybe one or two shots fired in that vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to make out what the situation is with the bottom window there, the bottom left-hand window?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There is glass in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there also glass out of it from what you can see?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No. I can't see from here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible -- I don't know whether it is possible with this Sanction to zoom in on it. Is that a facility we have, to zoom in on the bottom left-hand window? We'll just see what we can do, Ms. Adie, and --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: There was almost no broken glass anywhere. You are instantly conscious of broken glass in these circumstances because you watch where you put your feet and you are aware of crunching on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just -- okay. Sorry. Apparently we can't -- we can't get any resolution to that. Very well. Okay. Well, can we now press on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just stop for a moment please. I just ask that we go back to the previous person. There appeared to be a shoe and a whitish covering over a person, perhaps three or four seconds before. Before that. That's it. Thank you. Stop there, please. That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, now, pull the cover off that particular person or -- or sorry, did you have a chance to look at that particular person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I may have done. I do know that I looked at half a dozen bodies. I have to honestly tell you, I cannot now -- and there were several which we looked at that are not on the video because we have not got all the bodies that we found in the village on this video. We didn't film all of them, and I cannot honestly recall specifically which I looked at and which I did not. All I can say is that there was no inconsistency between all of the bodies I looked at, that they were all bullet wounds in elderly people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That one there, just let me ask you this: Do you recall whether or not you looked at that person --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I can't. I told you, I cannot recall the differences between them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the gender of that person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you recall. Geographical positioning of that person?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall anything about that one?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated that you looked at -- I think you said --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Six or seven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Six or seven.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "looked at," do you mean that you had a close look at those people and noticed what wounds was on them or --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you say -- and I think you're indicating that you've seen perhaps seven more than that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: We saw about I think a dozen or so. I have to be vague. I can't give you a number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So do I. But what I wanted to ask you was of the six or seven that we're talking about that you looked at, are they all depicted on this particular video or --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: No. No, that's the point. There is no correlation between those I looked at and those on the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just following on from that. Of the ones we've seen so far on the video, how many of those include the ones that you've looked at --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, my memory's gone on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I'll try and remind you. That's okay there's a bit of detail to go through. You recall that there was a lady lying on a nice carpet?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes, her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's one of the ones that --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And the one on the grass outside on the corner of that house, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So that's two?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't look at this one?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't look at the person that we saw at the start in the field?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Not in the field, no. There two in the fields, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks, okay. Let's press on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Stop there, please. Sorry, we'll need to go back to that one. Sorry. Stop there. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, having regard to that picture there, is that how you saw these two individuals?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the position they were in?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself descend down and move any of those calico-looking bags or other objects?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The male -- the person on the left appears on the photograph to be a male. Is that the way you saw it at the time?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN ADIE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
